primitives.name: Score Difference Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model Bayesian hierarchical model (rstan; 4 chains × 2500 iterations, 1500 warm-up; full Stan code in Appendix) for the home-minus-away score difference y_g ~ t_ν(a_diff(g) + eff_diff(g) + ha(g), σ_y), a Student-t likelihood with ν ~ Gamma(9, 0.5) for heavy tails.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'y_g': 'score difference in game g (points)', 'a_{\\text{diff}}(g)': 'ability difference between teams in game g (dimensionless)', '\\text{eff}_{\\text{diff}}(g)': 'effort difference in game g (dimensionless)', '\\text{ha}(g)': 'home advantage in game g (points)', '\\sigma_y': 'scale parameter for score difference (points)', '\\nu': 'degrees of freedom for Student-t distribution (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Ability changes slowly, effort proxy is derived from same-game scoring attempts, home advantage includes attendance effects.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When effort proxy becomes contaminated by outcome, model fails to distinguish true effort from score-driven behavior.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's state-space model of team strength and situational modifiers, enabling dynamic performance estimation.
layer2.telemetry: Posterior predictive score histogram matches empirical data.

primitives.name: Ability Random Walk
primitives.verbatim_quote: Features / target Features: per-team per-week ability (latent random walk, anchored on prior-season tries/points rankings), per-game effort ratios effH/effA (tries share of scoring attempts), attendance indicator, weekend-day indicator.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'a_{hw(g),ht(g)}': 'team ability in week h for team t in game g (dimensionless)', '\\sigma': 'standard deviation of ability innovation (dimensionless)', '\\eta_{hw(g),ht(g)}': 'Gaussian innovation term (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Team ability evolves gradually over time, innovations follow Gaussian distribution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If prior-season rankings are outdated or misaligned, random walk drifts from true ability.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's team strength evolution layer, where ability is updated weekly based on performance history.
layer2.telemetry: Trace plots confirm convergence of ability estimates.

primitives.name: Effort Proxy Ratio
primitives.verbatim_quote: Effort: eff_diff(g) = β_effort·(effH(g) - effA(g)); effH(g) = (home tries in g)/(home tries in g + attempted home scoring kicks in g), where attempted kicks = conversion opportunities + attempted penalties + attempted drops.
primitives.latex: \text{eff}_H(g) = \frac{\text{home tries in } g}{\text{home tries in } g + \text{attempted home scoring kicks in } g}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\text{eff}_H(g)': "home team's effort ratio in game g (dimensionless)", '\\text{home tries in } g': 'number of tries scored by home team in game g (count)', '\\text{attempted home scoring kicks in } g': 'total attempted kicks by home team in game g (count)'}
primitives.assumptions: Effort is proxied by the proportion of tries relative to all scoring attempts; assumes tries reflect aggressive playstyle.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When scoring structure varies significantly across games, proxy may misrepresent actual effort levels.

layer2.mapping: Mapped to GSE's aggressiveness metrics, but rejected due to target contamination; requires external validation.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation analysis shows independence from ability and home advantage.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core model defines score differences as a sum of ability, effort, and home advantage terms under a Student-t likelihood. The ability component uses a random walk with Gaussian innovations, anchoring on prior performance. Effort is modeled through a ratio of tries to total scoring attempts, which is problematic since it's derived from the same game being explained. This introduces target contamination, making effort a weak proxy. The home advantage includes attendance and day-of-week effects. Variance decomposition reveals equal contributions from ability, effort, and luck, suggesting balanced influence. The model's strength lies in its hierarchical structure and heavy-tailed error handling, but its reliance on a flawed effort measure limits its predictive utility. The Student-t distribution with estimated degrees of freedom provides robustness against outliers typical in sports data. Trace plots validate model identifiability, while posterior predictive checks ensure fit quality.
